extraction.name: VoiceAssistant-Eval
extraction.description: VoiceAssistant-Eval is a comprehensive benchmark of 10,497 curated instances across 13 task categories for evaluating AI assistants on listening, speaking, and viewing abilities. It includes tasks covering natural sounds, music, spoken dialogue, multi-turn dialogue, role-play imitation, and multimodal vision-audio integration.
extraction.creator: Ke Wang, Houxing Ren, Zimu Lu, Mingjie Zhan, Hongsheng Li
extraction.publisher: CUHK MMLab, SenseTime Research, CPII under InnoHK
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected from 23 audio understanding datasets and multiple text/audio datasets, organized into three subsets: Listening (audio clips with sounds, music, speech, and background noise), Speaking (spoken-interaction tasks with voice personalization), and Viewing (images paired with audio tasks). Text instructions were converted into audio for the benchmark.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Source data includes 23 audio understanding datasets (speech, sound, music, general categories), 22 additional datasets for the Speaking subset (11 text and 11 audio datasets), and MMMU for the Viewing subset, totaling 10,497 samples across diverse modalities.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Manual review by curators using a web-based curation tool, proceeding in three passes: (1) Media integrity check, (2) Task well-posedness check, (3) Answer validity check. Curators assign a Good or Bad verdict with optional notes. Human evaluation validation was also conducted where human judges independently evaluated 1050 sampled model responses.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom lightweight web-based curation tool built by the authors
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human evaluation validation conducted on 10% of model responses (1050 examples) across 13 tasks. Pearson correlation between automated (gpt-oss-20b) and human judgments ranged from 0.73 to 1.00 (overall 0.92). Agreement rate between automated and human evaluations was 96.1% overall, with several categories at 100%.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: One curator verdict per item during curation; independent human judges for validation evaluation
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Lexical overlap and Levenshtein distance for deduplication flagging; gpt-oss-20b used for automated evaluation scoring
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may carry biases from source data and design choices, drawn from academic or synthetic sources that might not reflect real deployment fairness concerns. The role-play subset uses a fixed set of 100 roles that may encode stereotypes or omit important user personas. GPT-based scoring may also introduce bias by favoring certain phrasings.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset has limited diversity (English-only except for five Chinese roles), limited model coverage (primarily open-source), automated evaluation that may introduce noise, gaps in task coverage (no video-audio integration or continuous streaming), and offline/static evaluation that does not capture real-world latency, barge-in, or error recovery scenarios.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark includes role-play voice imitation and speaker similarity evaluation, raising risks of identity spoofing, harassment, and fraud. Measures are in place to prohibit training models to reproduce identifiable speakers without consent, require consent gating and watermarking, and provide safety cards. The dataset also aims to minimize harms related to impersonation, privacy violations, and unequal performance across demographics.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset involves voice imitation and speaker similarity evaluation, which relates to identifiable speaker characteristics. Safeguards are in place regarding consent and anti-impersonation.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for evaluating voice assistants across listening, speaking, and viewing capabilities, and to facilitate future research in this area. It is not intended for training models for cheating. It is released under an MIT license for research use.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset and code will be publicly available under an MIT license. A data governance process will be maintained for auditing and removal, with the right to update assets if consent or licensing concerns arise.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Sampling was performed to balance the ratio of different tasks across 13 predefined categories, resulting in 10,497 high-quality samples. Speech synthesis was applied to question texts using three TTS models (F5TTS, ChatTTS, Dia-1.6B), with UTMOS Strong used to evaluate quality (score threshold >3.8) and Whisper-Large-v3 used to select audio with lowest word error rate.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Four-stage curation: (1) Deduplication using lexical overlap and Levenshtein distance with manual review, resulting in 15,359 samples; (2) Validation excluding corrupted images, silent audio, ill-posed prompts, and incorrect answers (~10% discarded); (3) Categorization into 13 predefined task categories; (4) Sampling to balance task ratios. For speech synthesis, text preprocessing included replacing image reference tokens with descriptive phrases, rewriting text with Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct for TTS suitability, and rephrasing multiple-choice options.

name.evidence: We introduce VoiceAssistant-Eval, a comprehensive benchmark designed to assess AI assistants across listening, speaking, and viewing.

description.evidence: VoiceAssistant-Eval comprises 10,497 curated examples spanning 13 task categories. These tasks include natural sounds, music, and spoken dialogue for listening; multi-turn dialogue, role-play imitation, and various scenarios for speaking; and highly heterogeneous images for viewing.

url.evidence: Code and data will be released at this page.

creator.evidence: Ke Wang1,∗Houxing Ren1,∗Zimu Lu1Mingjie Zhan2,†Hongsheng Li1,3,†

inLanguage.evidence: The paper is written in English and the benchmark uses English audio and text instructions throughout.

isLiveDataset.evidence: The final benchmark comprises roughly 10.5K carefully curated Q&A items.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: We collect source data from 23 audio understanding datasets, following the practice of AirBench (Yang et al., 2024)... The collected text instructions are then converted into audio.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: We collect source data from 23 audio understanding datasets... Other source data are from 22 datasets, including 11 text datasets... and 11 audio datasets.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: Tab. 8 provides an overview of the diverse set of source datasets included in our benchmark... Total 10497

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: Manual review proceeds in three quick passes: (1) Media integrity: Verify that the audio and images are present, decodable, audible, and visible, and that they are not silent or corrupted; (2) Task well-posedness: Confirm that the prompt is clear, unambiguous, and that inputs align with the stated task; (3) Answer validity: Check that reference answers are consistent with the prompt and media

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: we build a lightweight web-based curation tool that standardizes quality checks across modalities. The tool ingests candidate items consisting of a unique ID, metadata, raw prompt, reference answer(s), and associated media

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: All reported Pearson correlation coefficients between the model's scores and human ratings are notably high (ranging from 0.73 to 1.00, with an overall correlation of 0.92)... Agreement rate indicates the percentage of examples in which our model's evaluation matches that of the human evaluators... The overall agreement rate is 96.1%.

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: Curators review each item on a single screen... and then assign a Good or Bad verdict... These responses are then independently evaluated by human judges.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: We use lexical overlap and Levenshtein distance to flag potential duplicate questions... our automated model-based evaluation scheme (using gpt-oss-20b)

rai:dataBiases.evidence: like many benchmarks, VoiceAssistant-Eval may carry biases from its source data and design choices. The questions and contexts are drawn from academic or synthetic sources (e.g., existing datasets and rewritten instructions), which might not reflect the full richness or fairness concerns of real deployments. For example, the role-play subset uses a fixed set of 100 roles and associated style prompts. These roles may encode stereotypes or omit important user personas.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Although we include five Chinese roles in the role-play task, all other prompts and evaluations are in English. This monolingual focus may not capture the full variability of real user interactions... video-audio integration and continuous audio-visual streaming tasks are beyond the scope of this benchmark... VoiceAssistant-Eval evaluates models in an offline, static manner, which might not capture certain practical deployment factors.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: because the benchmark includes role-play voice imitation and speaker similarity evaluation, we emphasize strict consent, provenance, and anti-impersonation safeguards. To mitigate misuse risks (e.g., identity spoofing, harassment, fraud)... These measures aim to enable research on personalization while minimizing harms related to impersonation, privacy violations, and unequal performance across demographics.

rai:personalSensitiveInformation.evidence: because the benchmark includes role-play voice imitation and speaker similarity evaluation, we emphasize strict consent, provenance, and anti-impersonation safeguards... (i) prohibit training or releasing models intended to reproduce identifiable speakers without documented consent

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We intend for researchers to use this dataset to better evaluate voice assistants and, consequently, facilitate future studies in this area... The VoiceAssistant-Eval dataset is not supposed to be used, though the risk exists, for training models for cheating.

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: We will maintain a data governance process for auditing and removal and reserve the right to update assets if consent or licensing concerns arise... The VoiceAssistant-Eval data and our open-source code are under an MIT license.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: Sampling: We sample data from the categorized problems to balance the ratio of different tasks. After this, we obtain 10,497 high-quality samples.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: We improve data quality through a four-stage curation process: (1) Deduplication: We use lexical overlap and Levenshtein distance to flag potential duplicate questions... (2) Validation: We exclude incomplete or unsuitable instances, including entries with corrupted images, silent audio, ill-posed prompts, and demonstrably incorrect answers... (3) Categorization... (4) Sampling...
